findings.summary: Specification: 'the bound always fixes the output to well within its own magnitude' no longer holds now that tolF is about N/64*2^-22: at N=2^16 it needs attnAbs above about 4.4e-4.
findings.detail: README.md (Specification, after the table) says that at the largest covered values tolO is 24%, 'still below 1, so the bound always fixes the output to well within its own magnitude'. That reads only tolO. Since round 25, tolF is about N/64*2^-22, an absolute term that does not scale with v (work/tol.out: 3.34e-4 at D=256, N=2^16, X=2^10, and 2.5e-4 at X=16). So the bound is below attnAbs only when attnAbs > tolF/(1 - tolO), about 4.4e-4 (X=2^10) and 2.6e-4 (X=16) at N=2^16. tolF exceeds tolO*attnAbs when attnAbs is below 1.4e-3 to 1.2e-2 there, and below 3.6e-3 at the test's N=4096, X=23. HeadOk puts no lower bound on |v|. So a covered head whose v are all normal float16 values near 2^-12 gets a bound larger than its output. Before round 25 the threshold was about 4e-8, inside float16's subnormal range. On the host's v (randn times 0.5 or 1, attnAbs about 0.4 to 0.8), tolF is at most about 3% of tolO*attnAbs (D=256, N=2^16, X=16, s=0.5), and 0.9% at the test's sizes. So the tolerance stays meaningful in the kernel's real use. Resolve by qualifying the sentence: the bound fixes the output within its own magnitude when attnAbs is well above tolF. And say that tolF is the analysis's floor, not the device's, as r-fwd's F7 suggests. Wording; non-blocking.

findings.summary: absA's docstring puts relDot16 64 times the block's lift (5*2^-9) at 'about 1.5*2^-23'; it is 330*2^-31, about 1.29*2^-23.
findings.detail: Model.lean, absA's docstring: 'the p.v tl.dot's relDot16 64 = 66*2^-22 times the lift of a block's operands (... at most 5*2^-9 over the block's 64 keys ...), about 1.5*2^-23, with the roundings near zero'. The product is 66*5*2^-31 = 330*2^-31, about 1.29*2^-23 (work/check_lift.lean checks the value and that it is below absA = 2^-22, the margin covering the roundings that Step.astep's htau adds). The constant is sound. Only the figure in the words is off. Write 'about 1.3*2^-23', or 'below 1.5*2^-23'. Wording; non-blocking.

release.note: Settled by L126 (FIXED in round 25). It restates DotF16 and DotBF16 as DotLiftAcc, relative to |acc| + sum liftMag a*liftMag b, with a subnormal float16 operand counted at 2^-14, and its evidence is num-dot-sub16-round25 (a bit-exact model; the old bound failed by up to 113.7 times, the new bound's worst ratio is 0.111). This claim cites the restated fact as num.md lists it (assumption:dot = Rules.Num.DotF16 P). qk_lane (scoreMag) and pv_lane/astep (omega0, absA) use the lifted magnitude, including p.to(float16)'s subnormals.

notes: Round 3, gate df22d153664804d2 (library round 25, L126). assumption:dot is TVA.Rules.Num.DotF16 P, the fact num.md lists for tl.dot of float16 into float32 with maxImpreciseAcc 0 at any precision (cfg16 is tf32). It is now DotLiftAcc with relDot16 and absDot16 unchanged (work/check_lift.out prints the fields). The other eight assumption items were re-opened only through num.md, Num.lean and Sm90.lean. The facts they cite, and those facts' rows, are unchanged. The conditions item's digest is unchanged: HeadOk sits in spec. On the host's inputs, the lift adds at most 0.0059 (test) and 0.0305 (benchmark) to sigma*sum|q.k| (a chi-square tail, union bound over 2^22 rows, probability 2.6e-6), so sigma*scoreMag stays below 23 and 240, far under 2^10. My exact evaluation (work/tol.out) matches the README's table: tolO and tolM are unchanged, tolS grows 3.2%, and tolF is 1.5e-5, 6.4e-5 and 3.3e-4 at N = 4096, 2^14 and 2^16. On the host's data the tolerance stays meaningful at the largest covered sizes. I agree with r-fwd's F7: charged relative to p, the v lift would add about 66*2^-36 = 9.6e-10.
